fields.Back: A network of thousands of malware-compromised devices controlled by an attacker, used for spam distribution or distributed denial-of-service attacks.

fields.Text: The three categories of DoS attack: {{c1::vulnerability attacks}}, {{c2::bandwidth flooding}}, and {{c3::connection flooding}}.
fields.Extra: Vulnerability: a few crafted messages crash a service. Bandwidth flooding: packets clog the access link. Connection flooding: many half-open TCP connections.

fields.Front: What is a DDoS attack and why is it harder to defend against?
fields.Back: A distributed DoS: the attacker controls multiple sources (e.g., a botnet) that each blast traffic at the target; the aggregate reaches the victim's access rate R, and many sources are harder to detect and block than one.

fields.Front: What is a packet sniffer, and what is the main defence?
fields.Back: A passive receiver that records a copy of every packet on a broadcast medium (WiFi, cable, shared Ethernet); hard to detect because it injects nothing. Defence: cryptography.

fields.Text: Injecting packets with a false source address is called {{c1::IP spoofing}}; the defence is {{c2::end-point authentication}}.
